title: Package tree
subDomain: totalling weight and volume of nested cartons

act2.summary: a new node kind (a pallet, with its own tare weight added to totalWeight but not totalVolume) and a new traversal (totalItemCount) arrive together

solutions.title: Polymorphic node objects, one class per kind
solutions.tradeoff: A new node kind is one new class satisfying the existing interface - cheap, and the classic Composite strength. But a new operation means adding a method to the interface and implementing it in every class, including the brand-new one: this act 2 asks for both at once, and this route pays the expensive side of both trades simultaneously.

solutions.title: One visitor object per operation, dispatch by node kind
solutions.tradeoff: A new operation is one new visitor object, no existing code touched - the classic Visitor strength. But a new node kind means adding a method to the visitor interface and implementing it in every existing visitor: this act 2 asks for both at once, and this route pays the expensive side of both trades simultaneously, same as Composite from the other direction.

solutions.title: One generic fold, two callbacks passed at each call site
solutions.tradeoff: Neither a new node kind nor a new operation has a dedicated place to attach to - both mean touching the one fold function and every call site that uses it, in a single contiguous edit. That costs more total lines than the no-pattern baseline's scattered edits, but far fewer separate hunks: the whole change lands in one place instead of three.

reviewFocus: Does the chosen candidate's WALKTHROUGH.md name what would change my mind about the choice, or does it just describe the code?
In the composite route, is PalletNode's weight() really the only place tare weight can leak in, or could a bug hide it somewhere else in the class?

In the visitor route, does every one of the three visitor objects (weight, volume, itemCount) implement visitPallet correctly - two of them should ignore the tare entirely, and it's easy to copy-paste the one that doesn't

Is 'this act 2 asks for both a new node kind and a new operation, which is exactly the axis each pattern was not built to protect' a fair reading of why plain recursion wins here - and would a reader's CHOICE.md, written before act 2, have said the same thing?
Do all three routes - and the no-pattern baseline - agree, byte for byte, on totalWeight, totalVolume and totalItemCount for the same tree, pallets included?
